title: How Ukraine Put Russia on the Backfoot
gist: A short podcast episode blurb asserting that Ukraine's expanding use of drones across all ranges has shifted the momentum of the war, enabling deeper strikes into Russian territory against operations, logistics, and energy infrastructure. The page poses but does not answer whether these strikes yield durable battlefield advantage or push Russia toward escalation.

insights.claim: Ukraine's expanding use of drones across all ranges has changed the momentum of the war with Russia, allowing Kyiv to reach deeper into Russian territory against operations, logistics, and energy infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Michael Kofman, Dara Massicot, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Sustained drone strikes on Russian energy infrastructure are a live supply-side risk to Russian refining and crude export throughput.
insights.quote: Ukraine’s expanding use of drones at all ranges has changed the war’s momentum.

insights.claim: Whether Ukrainian deep strikes can produce lasting battlefield advantages, and whether they will force Russia to escalate, are treated as open questions rather than settled outcomes by analysts Michael Kofman and Dara Massicot.
insights.speaker: Michael Kofman, Dara Massicot, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Even sympathetic expert analysts are not underwriting durable Ukrainian advantage — a caution against extrapolating headline strike successes into a trend.
insights.quote: Can these strikes produce lasting advantages on the battlefield? Will this force Russia to escalate?

insights.claim: Russia's capacity to adapt to Ukraine's deep-strike drone campaign is explicitly framed as uncertain, with the possibility that it is not adapting at all left open.
insights.speaker: Michael Kofman, Dara Massicot, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Russian counter-drone adaptation speed is the key variable determining how long Russian energy-infrastructure disruption persists.
insights.locator: This episode examines how Kyiv is reaching deeper

source_meta.author: Michael Kofman, Dara Massicot, and Ryan Evans
